calls.head: A shadow job for Bertuzzi, Frondell and Greenway
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Bertuzzi’s line (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Greenway) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Panarin, Laferriere and Kempe.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Blackhawks squeak past the Kings
paras: Samuel Helenius opened the scoring for the Kings early in the first, and that was all they would get. The Kings went nearly 17 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the first to early in the second, even with a power play in that stretch. Roman Kantserov made it 1-1 for Chicago on the power play late in the second, and Wyatt Kaiser put the Blackhawks ahead for good early in the third.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Spencer Knight made 25 saves for the Blackhawks, and Anton Forsberg kept the Kings in it, stopping 25 of 27. The Hawks improved to 4-8-0, still last in the Central, while the Kings fell to 3-6-2, seventh in the Pacific.

items.text: The Blackhawks won for the first time in four games.
Wyatt Kaiser scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 20 (24 games played since).

The Kings were without Kevin Fiala, Alex Turcotte, Drew Doughty and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Capitals and the Penguins were missing more at the time.
Patrick Kane is now one assist from 900.
